column1: # H.264 Extended profile streams, self-generated for H264ExtendedProfileTest. Columns:
# name
# Every stream but si-model and si-model-cip was encoded with the JM reference encoder 19.1 (lencod, jvet/JM
# master, built from source with MinGW gcc 15.2 after tools/testdata/h264-extended/patch-jm.py; make-vectors.py
# there regenerates every stream and hash) from its cfg/encoder_extended.cfg (ProfileIDC=88) with LevelIDC=30 and
# the parameters below. The input is ffmpeg 7.1's "testsrc2=size=176x144:rate=25,noise=alls=10:allf=t+u" as yuv420p,
# except dp-pcm, whose right 64 columns carry "noise=alls=100:allf=t+u" (clipped to 16..235 and 16..240) so that
# they code as I_PCM, and dp-mbaff, dp-field and sp-mbaff-dp, which use
# "testsrc2=size=176x144:rate=50,tinterlace=mode=merge,noise=alls=8:allf=t+u". sp-switch codes its SP pictures as
# switching pictures (sp_for_switch_flag) from the coefficients sp-coefficients wrote (SP_output=1); si codes SI
# slices, whose macroblocks lencod always makes I macroblocks.
# The expected frame hashes in frames.tsv (MD5 of each frame as planar 8-bit 4:2:0) of these streams are the output
# of the JM 19.1 decoder (ldecod) patched where it departs from ITU-T H.264 8.6: it pairs the chroma DC levels of SP
# and SI macroblocks with the transposed prediction DC coefficients, and requantizes with the slice QP instead of the
# macroblock's QPY and QPC and without chroma_qp_index_offset for QSC. The patched decoder reproduces the reference
# YUV of the conformance streams SP1_BT_A and sp2_bt_b frame for frame, where the unpatched one does not. It also
# reproduces the encoder's reconstruction of every stream without SP or SI slices and of sp-coefficients and
# sp-switch; the encoder's reconstruction of the other SP and SI streams differs, because lencod codes the intra
# macroblocks of SP and SI slices with the SP requantization, which the standard does not apply to them.
# si-model and si-model-cip hold SI macroblocks, which lencod never writes and ldecod cannot decode unpatched. They
# are written bit by bit by tools/testdata/h264-extended/make-si-streams.py, and their expected frames come from
# its model of ITU-T H.264 8.3 and 8.6.2; the patched ldecod agrees with the model on si-model (it does not apply
# the SI rule of constrained_intra_pred_flag that si-model-cip exercises).
